doc.title: Steve Davis interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, December 15, 2017

title: Introduction: trombonist, composer, educator
summary: Davis introduces himself as a musician who plays trombone, composes and teaches.

story.theme_name: Opening the interview: Monk Rowe's welcome and archive boilerplate
story.community_name: Opening the Hamilton College interview: introductions and boilerplate

blocks.x: My name is Monk Rowe and I’m happy to have Steve Davis with me today for the Fillius Jazz Archive. And I was going to introduce you as, you know, what you do, but I thought I’d let you do that. Because as a musician you probably wear many hats.

Yeah. Twelve bucks on Canal Street in New York. Well I play the trombone. I’m a musician who happens to play the trombone. I love jazz music, I have since I was a teenager. I compose music as well. I’m an educator, and, you know, very interested in many things in life, not just music, but that’s been kind of my main area, certainly, of employment, and my life’s work is involved in playing music and writing music and teaching music.
Is there one of those things that is the most important to you?
